Class ColorUtil

java.lang.Object
net.murat.util.ColorUtil
public final class ColorUtil extends Object
Utility class for RGB color operations. All methods work exclusively with packed integer ARGB colors to eliminate object allocation. Format: (A << 24) | (R << 16) | (G << 8) | B Compatible with Java 6-8 without lambdas.

    • interpolate

      public static int interpolate(int colorA, int colorB, float t)
      Energy-conserving linear interpolation between two packed ARGB colors. Used for reflection compositing: result = local * (1 - t) + reflected * t Unlike ColorUtil.add(), this does not double-count light energy when blending a surface's local lighting with its reflected contribution.
      Parameters:
      colorA - base/local color (used when t = 0)
      colorB - blend/reflected color (used when t = 1)
      t - blend factor, clamped to [0, 1] (typically the material's reflectivity)
      Returns:
      packed ARGB result with alpha forced to 0xFF

      public static int tint(int source, int tint)
      Tints the source color with the tint color using channel-wise multiplication. This simulates a colored filter effect - like looking through colored glass.
      Parameters:
      source - The original color (e.g., refracted ray color from behind the object)
      tint - The tinting color (e.g., material's own color)
      Returns:
      The tinted color, with alpha preserved from the source

    • applyTint

      public static int applyTint(int source, int tint, float strength)
      Applies a tint to a color by blending toward the tint color. This preserves luminance while shifting hue - unlike multiply which darkens.
      Parameters:
      source - The original color (0xAARRGGBB)
      tint - The tint color to apply (0xAARRGGBB)
      strength - The tint strength (0.0 = no tint, 1.0 = full tint)
      Returns:
      Tinted color with original alpha preserved
